evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends MFA across account types to reduce abuse of compromised valid credentials.

evidence.statement: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate unprivileged human users of systems.

mappings.rationale: Requiring MFA for unprivileged system users may prevent abuse of Valid Accounts (T1078) when an adversary has obtained a password but cannot satisfy the additional factor.
mappings.relationship_description: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) across all account types, including default, local, domain, and cloud accounts, to prevent unauthorized access, even if credentials are compromised. MFA provides a critical layer of security by requiring multiple forms of verification beyond just a password. This measure significantly reduces the risk of adversaries abusing valid accounts to gain initial access, escalate privileges, maintain persistence, or evade defenses within your network.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends MFA across account types to reduce abuse of compromised valid credentials.

evidence.statement: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate privileged human users of systems.

mappings.rationale: Requiring MFA for privileged system users may prevent privileged Valid Accounts (T1078) from being abused with a compromised password alone.
mappings.relationship_description: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) across all account types, including default, local, domain, and cloud accounts, to prevent unauthorized access, even if credentials are compromised. MFA provides a critical layer of security by requiring multiple forms of verification beyond just a password. This measure significantly reduces the risk of adversaries abusing valid accounts to gain initial access, escalate privileges, maintain persistence, or evade defenses within your network.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends gateways and similar mechanisms to limit unnecessary remote access to sensitive systems.

evidence.statement: Administrative activities are conducted through jump servers.

mappings.mitigation_name: Limit Access to Resource Over Network
mappings.rationale: Routing administrative activity through jump servers constrains Remote Services (T1021) by limiting direct network paths to managed administrative gateways.
mappings.relationship_description: Prevent unnecessary remote access to file shares, hypervisors, sensitive systems, etc. Mechanisms to limit access may include use of network concentrators, RDP gateways, etc.(Citation: Sygnia ESXi Ransomware 2024)

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK states that ad blockers can prevent malicious code served through advertisements from executing.

evidence.statement: Web browsers do not process web advertisements from the internet.

mappings.rationale: Blocking internet advertisements in browsers may prevent the malicious-advertising delivery path used by Drive-by Compromise (T1189).
mappings.relationship_description:
Adblockers can help prevent malicious code served through ads from executing in the first place. Script blocking extensions can also help to prevent the execution of JavaScript. 

Consider disabling browser push notifications from certain applications and browsers.(Citation: mac security virus popup)(Citation: push notifications -infosecinstitute)(Citation: site notifications - krebsonsecurity)

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends MFA across account types to reduce abuse of compromised valid credentials.

evidence.statement: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to their organisation’s online services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive data.

mappings.rationale: MFA on organisational online services processing sensitive data may prevent access through compromised Valid Accounts (T1078) when only a password is available.
mappings.relationship_description: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) across all account types, including default, local, domain, and cloud accounts, to prevent unauthorized access, even if credentials are compromised. MFA provides a critical layer of security by requiring multiple forms of verification beyond just a password. This measure significantly reduces the risk of adversaries abusing valid accounts to gain initial access, escalate privileges, maintain persistence, or evade defenses within your network.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends MFA, including on externally facing services, as a mitigation for brute force.

evidence.statement: Multi-factor authentication is used to authenticate human users to their organisation’s online services that process, store or communicate their organisation’s sensitive data.

mappings.rationale: MFA on organisational online services may prevent Brute Force (T1110) from yielding access when password guessing succeeds but the additional factor is unavailable.
mappings.relationship_description: Use multi-factor authentication. Where possible, also enable multi-factor authentication on externally facing services.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends regular, tested, protected backups to restore data after encryption for impact.

evidence.statement: Backups of data, applications and settings are performed and retained in accordance with business criticality and business continuity requirements.

mappings.rationale: Performing and retaining business-aligned backups supports recovery after Data Encrypted for Impact (T1486) by preserving restorable copies.
mappings.relationship_description: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for regularly taking and testing data backups that can be used to restore organizational data.(Citation: Ready.gov IT DRP) Ensure backups are stored off system and is protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and destroy the backups to prevent recovery. Consider enabling versioning in cloud environments to maintain backup copies of storage objects.(Citation: Rhino S3 Ransomware Part 2)

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK specifically identifies PowerShell Constrained Language Mode as restricting dangerous PowerShell language elements.

evidence.statement: PowerShell is configured to use Constrained Language Mode.

mappings.rationale: PowerShell Constrained Language Mode constrains PowerShell (T1059.001) by restricting dangerous language elements and arbitrary Windows API access.
mappings.relationship_description: Use application control where appropriate. PowerShell Constrained Language mode can be used to restrict access to sensitive or otherwise dangerous language elements such as those used to execute arbitrary Windows APIs or files (e.g., `Add-Type`).(Citation: Microsoft PowerShell CLM)

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK states application control may prevent executables masquerading as other files from running.

evidence.statement: Application control restricts the execution of executables, libraries, scripts, installers, compiled HTML, HTML applications and control panel applets to an organisation-approved set.

mappings.rationale: Restricting executables and scripts to an approved set may prevent a Malicious File (T1204.002) from running after user execution.
mappings.relationship_description: Application control may be able to prevent the running of executables masquerading as other files.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK states antivirus can automatically quarantine suspicious files used for Visual Basic execution.

evidence.statement: Microsoft Office macro antivirus scanning is enabled.

mappings.rationale: Enabling antivirus scanning for Office macros may prevent malicious Visual Basic (T1059.005) macro code by detecting and quarantining the containing file.
mappings.relationship_description: Anti-virus can be used to automatically quarantine suspicious files.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK identifies Credential Guard as protecting LSA secrets while noting incomplete coverage of credential dumping.

mappings.rationale: Credential Guard constrains LSASS Memory (T1003.001) credential dumping by isolating LSA secrets, although ATT&CK notes it does not stop every dumping method.
mappings.relationship_description: With Windows 10, Microsoft implemented new protections called Credential Guard to protect the LSA secrets that can be used to obtain credentials through forms of credential dumping. It is not configured by default and has hardware and firmware system requirements. It also does not protect against all forms of credential dumping.(Citation: TechNet Credential Guard)(Citation: GitHub SHB Credential Guard)

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends patch management for externally exposed applications.

evidence.statement: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in online services are applied within two weeks of release when vulnerabilities are assessed as non-critical by vendors and no working exploits exist.

mappings.rationale: Applying vendor fixes to online services within the stated window may prevent Exploit Public-Facing Application (T1190) against vulnerabilities covered by those fixes.
mappings.relationship_description: Update software regularly by employing patch management for externally exposed applications.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends patch management for internal enterprise endpoints and servers.

evidence.statement: Patches, updates or other vendor mitigations for vulnerabilities in operating systems of workstations, non-internet-facing servers and non-internet-facing network devices are applied within one month of release.

mappings.rationale: Patching workstation, internal-server, and network-device operating systems may prevent Exploitation of Remote Services (T1210) where the exploited flaw is covered by the update.
mappings.relationship_description: Update software regularly by employing patch management for internal enterprise endpoints and servers.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends off-system backups protected from adversary access and destruction.

evidence.statement: Privileged user accounts (excluding backup administrator accounts) are prevented from modifying and deleting backups.

mappings.rationale: Preventing ordinary privileged accounts from modifying or deleting backups constrains Data Destruction (T1485) by preserving recovery copies outside those accounts’ reach.
mappings.relationship_description: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for taking regular data backups that can be used to restore organizational data.(Citation: Ready.gov IT DRP) Ensure backups are stored off system and protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and destroy the backups to prevent recovery.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends off-system backups protected from adversary access and destruction.

evidence.statement: Backups of data, applications and settings are retained in a secure and resilient manner.

mappings.rationale: Secure and resilient retention of backups supports recovery after Data Destruction (T1485) by preserving organisational data outside the destructive event.
mappings.relationship_description: Consider implementing IT disaster recovery plans that contain procedures for taking regular data backups that can be used to restore organizational data.(Citation: Ready.gov IT DRP) Ensure backups are stored off system and protected from common methods adversaries may use to gain access and destroy the backups to prevent recovery.

evidence.relationship_summary: ATT&CK recommends enabling Protected Process Light for LSA against LSASS memory credential dumping.

evidence.statement: Local Security Authority protection functionality is enabled.

mappings.rationale: Enabling Local Security Authority protection constrains LSASS Memory (T1003.001) dumping by running LSA as a protected process.
mappings.relationship_description: On Windows 8.1 and Windows Server 2012 R2, enable Protected Process Light for LSA.(Citation: Microsoft LSA)
